1. 갈라디아서 기록 배경\n - 사도바울이 여행 중에 몸이 편치 잠깐:
1. Background of Galatians
 - While the apostle Paul was traveling, he wasn't well and rested for a while, and the churches planted during that time are the churches of Galatia.
 -  We think many churches were planted. Verse 2: 'unto the churches'
핵심 내용은 이렇습니다. 전에 바울이 개척했던 갈라디아 지역에 할례파 사: The core of it is this. People from the circumcision party came into the region of Galatia, where Paul had planted churches earlier, and preached a bogus gospel. 'Sure, you're saved by believing in Jesus, but before that you have to get circumcised and become a Jew, and then believe in Jesus.' They're spouting this kind of garbage, and the Galatians actually went and got circumcised. Trying to be saved...(Remember how earlier the Bereans searched the Scriptures to see whether it was really true?)
뿐만 아니라 ‘바울은 사도가 아니다’하면서 사도성을 의심 하는거예요. 이: And not only that, they say 'Paul is not an apostle,' casting doubt on his apostleship. When Paul heard this news he got angry, and the letter he wrote is Galatians. Right from verse 1 he blows up, doesn't he?
<갈1:1~3> 사람들에게서 난 것도 아니요 사람으로 말미암은 것도 아니:
<Gal 1:1~3> Paul, an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead;) And all the brethren which are with me, unto the churches of Galatia: Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ
 - His apostleship isn't the kind that gets recognized by people; it was recognized by God.
<갈1:6~7> 그리스도의 은혜로 너희를 부르신 이를 이같이 속히 떠나: <Gal 1:6~7> I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.
내가 전한 복음 외에 다른 복음은 없다. 그 할례파 사람들은 복음을 변하: There's no other gospel besides the gospel I preached. Those circumcision people are doing this to twist the gospel.
<갈1:8~9> 그러나 우리나 혹 하늘로부터 온 천사라도 우리가 너희에게: <Gal 1:8~9> But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.
천사라고 할지라도 내가 전한 진짜 복음 외에 딴소리 하면 저주를 받을거다: Even if it's an angel, if he says anything other than the real gospel I preached, he'll be cursed.
그 다음에 바울이 사도가 된 경위를 주욱 설명 - 내가 전에는 하나님의: Next Paul explains at length how he became an apostle - "I used to persecute God's church severely, and I was so extreme in Judaism, more zealous than my ancestors, but then I met Jesus, the very one I'd been persecuting."
그 때 사도들에게도, 혈육들에게도 의논하지 않았다. 그렇게 다메섹으로 갔: "At that time I didn't consult the apostles or my own flesh and blood. I went to Damascus like that, went up to Jerusalem after 3 years, and went through the regions of Syria and Cilicia."
그 후, 14년이 지나서 예루살렘으로 돌아왔는데 그 때도 사도들의 명성에: "After that, 14 years later, I came back to Jerusalem, and even then I didn't lean on the apostles' reputation to preach the gospel. Why? So that my efforts wouldn't be in vain..."
그리고 디도 얘기를 하는데요, 디도가 헬라인이잖아요? 이방인인데도 내가: And he talks about Titus. Titus was a Greek, right? "Even though he was a Gentile, I didn't do anything like forcing him to be circumcised. Because of those guys who quietly sneaked in, I made a point of not doing it." He says things like that.
그리고 바울이 받은 계시는 다른 사도들과 똑같이 예수님께 직접 받은 것이: And Paul strongly stresses that the revelation he received came directly from Jesus, just like the other apostles. Verse 7 - just as Peter was sent to the circumcised, I was sent to the uncircumcised. Peter was sent to the Jews, Paul to the Gentiles.
이어서 ‘내가 베드로의 외식을 책망 한 적도 있다. 베드로면 다인줄 아냐: Then he says, 'I even rebuked Peter for his hypocrisy once. Do you think being Peter means he gets a pass?' — see, earlier Peter was eating with Gentiles, and when the circumcision party came in, he pretended he hadn't been eating, pretended he didn't know those people, and slipped away. It even says Barnabas was led astray seeing that...
그러면서 바울은 ‘사람이 의롭게 되는 것이 율법을 잘 지켜서 되는 게 아: And so Paul lays out his argument: 'A person isn't made righteous by keeping the law well, but by believing in Jesus.' You don't become righteous by doing things like circumcision.
1절. 예수님께서 돌아가신지 얼마 되지도 않아서 아직 눈에 선한데 벌써: Verse 1. Jesus died not long ago, it's still vivid before your eyes, so how can you already be wavering like this?
2절 - 이 사람들이 할례받지 않았을 때 이미 성령을 받았거든요? 그래서: Verse 2 - These people had already received the Holy Spirit when they weren't circumcised, right? So Paul asks: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, by getting circumcised? Didn't you already receive the Spirit before you were circumcised? Are you that foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now trying to finish in the flesh, huh? He lets them have it, fiercely.
And after that, he has a word for those who stress the works of the law. Look at verse 10: those who try to get somewhere by keeping the law — if you're going to keep it, you have to keep all of it. But is it possible to keep it all? Impossible! Before God, no one can keep the law perfectly. That's why Christ took our place and bore the curse we should have received, and now we've become free people. So please, don't listen to anyone saying you have to get circumcised or anything like that.
15절부터 중요한 개념을 말합니다. 하나님께서 아브라함에게 하신 약속이: From verse 15 he talks about an important idea. God made a promise to Abraham, and that promise was settled before the law came, 430 years earlier. So can the law, given a full 430 years later, override that promise? No, it can't, he says.
그럼 율법은 왜 주셨느냐? 자꾸 죄를 지으니까. 그래서 이 율법의 기능은: Then why was the law given? Because people kept sinning. So the role of the law is to be a schoolmaster leading us until Jesus came. To put it simply, the law is a set of guidelines given because people kept sinning, until the one who would solve all of it came.
그런데 이제 그 예수님이 오셨기 때문에 율법이 하라는 대로 할 것이 아니: But now that Jesus has come, we shouldn't do as the law says; we should do as Jesus says. Anyone who has been baptized into Christ has put on Christ. That's the point.
4장에서 다시 설명하는데 주인에게 자식이 있다. 근데 어려. 그러니까 아: In chapter 4 he explains it again: a master has a son. But he's young. So the father puts a steward over him and entrusts the son to him until he grows up. But when the time came, God sent His Son, made of a woman, made under the law — and why? To put Him in the same situation as us, so that we could receive the adoption of sons. So we became sons of God. And if you're a son? You have the right to the inheritance.
하나님께서 이렇게까지 하셔서 우리에게 주시려는 것은 5장입니다. 바로 자: What God wants to give us by going this far is chapter 5. It's freedom, that's what. Freedom. Therefore, never again put on the yoke of slavery. If you get circumcised, all this work of Christ does that person no good. Look at verse 3. Like I said earlier, a person like that? Has to keep the whole law.
11절 바울이 만약에 할례 문제를 적당히 타협하고 넘어 갔으면 이렇게까지: Verse 11: if Paul had just compromised a bit on the circumcision issue and let it slide, he wouldn't have been persecuted this much. And then he says, if you're so set on that petty little snip, go do it to yourselves. Don't go hanging around the circumcision party for it.
그럼 어떻게 해야 하냐? 16절부터 보시면 성령을 따라 행하라. 그러면: So then what should we do? Look from verse 16: walk in the Spirit. Then you won't fulfill the lusts of the flesh. What are the lusts of the flesh? Verse 19. Fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness, idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies, envyings, drunkenness, revellings.. things like these. People who do these things won't enter the kingdom of God.
성령의 열매는 사랑, 희락, 화평, 오래 참음, 자비, 양선, 충성, 온: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance
Verse 26: Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.
제가 우리 애들에게 제일 많이 하는 말이예요. 자존심 조금 상하게 했다고: This is what I say to my kids most often. Don't get irritated and jealous with each other just because someone hurt your pride a little.
The last one, chapter 6. After saying all this, Paul seems to have gotten a little worried. That people who weren't circumcised yet would criticize the ones who already had been, and the church would get torn apart...
그래서 권면하기를 1절입니다. “형제들아 사람이 만일 무슨 범죄한 일이: So he urges them, verse 1: "Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted."
다른 사람이 범죄한 것을 알게 되거든 온유한 심령으로 바로 잡아주어야지: If you find out someone else has sinned, you should restore them with a gentle spirit; if you point it out and puff yourself up feeling superior, the church breaks apart right away. And not only that, you have to look at yourself and be careful not to commit the same sin. In that way we bear one another's burdens, and at the same time each one has to examine his own work.
Finally Paul adds one more word, verse 11.
“내가 이렇게 큰 글자로 쓴 것을 보라” 바울의 친필은 글씨가 크고 악필: "See with what large letters I have written unto you" It's said that Paul's own handwriting was big and messy. Anyway, what he wanted to say is this: those circumcision people are bad guys, so don't listen to them. Them going around circumcising people? It's all so they can brag about themselves, not a pure motive. And those guys are happy to go around doing circumcisions, but they don't keep the law one bit. From now on, please don't trouble me. You can't find a single mark of suffering on them, but I bear the marks of Jesus.
“우리 주 예수 그리스도의 은혜가 너희 심령에 있을찌어다. 아멘.” 하면: "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen." — and with that the letter ends.
Still, he ends on a gentle note, doesn't he?  Now we go back to Acts 18:12....
